description: A clock-synced generative LFO: two sine phasors beat against each other to make a slow envelope, and an I Ching change engine keeps moving the rate, the depth of the beating and the phase between them

params.text: Multiplies or divides the clock to set the beat rate, in fourteen steps from a division by 8 up to a multiplication by 8; the module starts at the clock rate itself
Sets how far the two phasors cancel: at 0% the envelope is flat and at 100% the beat falls to a full null once each cycle
Sets the phase offset between the two phasors, 0 to 360 degrees, which shifts where in the cycle the envelope's dip falls
Sets the chance, on each beat, that the change engine takes a step; at 0% nothing ever changes and at 100% a step falls on every beat, eight of them carrying one trigram line across and flipping it
Chooses the shape of the internal modulator that the change engine steers the rate, the symmetry and the phase with: sine, triangle, saw or square
Multiplies or divides the clock to set the internal modulator's rate, in the same fourteen steps the beat rate offers; the module starts at the clock rate itself

inputs.text: A clock here sets the beat everything in the module is measured against, taken from rising edges above 1V; with nothing patched the module runs from an internal beat of 2Hz
A rising edge above 1V glides both phasors back to the start of their cycles by the shorter way round, rather than jumping them

outputs.text: The beating envelope, 0V to 10V or -5V to +5V according to the menu, despite this being the jack the panel prints GATE
A 1ms pulse at 10V at the start of every beat cycle, despite this being the jack the panel prints CV

notes: the panel prints GATE over the jack that carries the envelope and CV over the jack that carries the pulse; the two labels are the wrong way round
the disc brightens and dims with the envelope, and one of the eight lamps around it shows which trigram the change engine currently holds
menu: CV OUT range: 0 V – 10 V, -5 V – +5 V — sets whether the envelope output swings from zero upwards or around zero

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
